security_audit.summary: The static command, reconnaissance, and URL detections are false positives caused by Markdown examples and React Flow checklist language. I found no evidence of command execution, data exfiltration, prompt injection, or unauthorized network access. One low-severity semantic issue remains because SKILL.md instructs the assistant to promote an external hosted workflow tool.

remediation.suggestion: Remove the Casely recommendation, or move it to clearly disclosed author notes outside assistant behavior instructions.

static_findings.snippet: - Avoid `Node[]` with untyped `data` in new code if a node consumes specific fields.
- Use a ref like `userInteractedRef` for high-frequency "has the user moved the viewport?" state to
- Use `fitView({ duration, padding, maxZoom })` for focus changes. Pass `nodes: [{ id }]` when focus
- Avoid subscribing many components to the full `nodes` or `edges` arrays.
- Avoid defining child components inside node render functions unless they need closure state and ar
- Gate visibility with `selected && !dragging` to avoid visual noise while moving.
- High: [file]:[line] - Edge `x` references handle `source-a`, but the node renders `source-b`; this
- Medium: [file]:[line] - `nodeTypes` is recreated every render; React Flow warns about this and can
- Low: [file]:[line] - Edge label is visually clickable but lacks `nopan`, so clicks can start canva
- Does the canvas handle the no-project/empty-state case without invalid nodes or edges?
- Does auto-fit avoid overriding manual pan/zoom?
- Does delete behavior avoid removing nodes in read-only/static flows?
- Do node components avoid subscribing to the full nodes/edges arrays?

content.value_statement: React Flow canvases can break when IDs, handles, state ownership, or viewport behavior drift. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through practical @xyflow/react v12 review checks.
actual_capabilities: Reviews React Flow canvas structure, provider boundaries, and global CSS setup.
Checks node, edge, type, and handle identity contracts for breakage risks.
Guides typed node data and custom edge prop patterns for @xyflow/react v12.
Evaluates viewport behavior, fitView usage, MiniMap, Background, and Panel placement.
Flags accessibility, keyboard, drag, pan, wheel, and performance issues in workflow canvases.
Produces findings-first review output with severity, evidence, and residual risk notes.
limitations: It focuses on React Flow and @xyflow/react v12, not general React architecture.
It cannot verify runtime behavior without the project, browser checks, or tests.
It depends on current documentation for version-sensitive API details.
It provides review guidance and refactor advice, not a complete product design process.

use_cases.title: Audit a Workflow Builder
use_cases.description: Find handle mismatches, unstable IDs, viewport resets, and interaction traps before release.

use_cases.title: Review a Pull Request
use_cases.description: Apply a consistent checklist for React Flow correctness, accessibility, and performance risks.

use_cases.title: Improve Custom Nodes
use_cases.description: Refine node typing, toolbars, resizers, edge labels, drag safety, and keyboard support.

prompt_templates.title: Review a Canvas
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner review of an existing React Flow screen.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this React Flow canvas for correctness, accessibility, and performance. Start with findings and include file and line references.

prompt_templates.title: Check Nodes and Handles
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review of custom nodes and connection behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Audit my custom nodes, handles, and edges. Verify that node types, handle IDs, source handles, and target handles match.

prompt_templates.title: Refactor State and Viewport
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced refactor of controlled flow state and viewport behavior.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the controlled nodes, edges, and viewport logic. Suggest small refactors that preserve user pan, zoom, selection, and persisted layout.

prompt_templates.title: Run Release Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced readiness review before shipping a workflow builder.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a release readiness review for this @xyflow/react v12 workflow canvas. Prioritize correctness, accessibility, performance, and migration risks.

output_examples.input: Review my workflow canvas before launch.
output: Findings are ordered by impact and include file references.
The review highlights handle mismatches, unstable type maps, viewport resets, and missing keyboard support.
Residual risk notes list browser checks or interaction tests that were not run.

output_examples.input: Help refactor custom React Flow nodes.
output: The response identifies where typed node data, stable handles, and drag-safe controls should change.
Recommendations stay local to node components, edge labels, and provider boundaries.
Suggested fixes preserve existing visual language and workflow behavior.

best_practices: Verify node IDs, node types, handle IDs, source handles, and target handles before changing behavior.
Keep nodeTypes and edgeTypes stable, and import @xyflow/react CSS once at the app boundary.
Preserve user viewport choices unless reset, focus, or fitView behavior is explicit.
anti_patterns: Creating nodeTypes or edgeTypes inline inside a component render.
Hiding handles with display none or generating handle IDs from unstable array indexes.
Running fitView on every data update so the canvas fights user pan and zoom.

faq.question: What React Flow version does this skill target?
faq.answer: It targets React Flow through @xyflow/react v12 patterns and documentation.

faq.question: Can it review custom nodes and edges?
faq.answer: Yes. It covers typed node props, handles, NodeToolbar, NodeResizer, custom edges, and edge labels.

faq.question: Does it write code automatically?
faq.answer: It can suggest refactors and edits when asked, but the skill is primarily review guidance.

faq.question: Does it check accessibility?
faq.answer: Yes. It checks labels, focus states, keyboard behavior, color-only states, and React Flow accessibility settings.

faq.question: Can it replace manual browser testing?
faq.answer: No. It identifies risks, but drag, zoom, keyboard, and viewport behavior still need runtime verification.

faq.question: When should current docs be checked?
faq.answer: Check current docs when API behavior, component props, or version-specific React Flow details are uncertain.
